spot: The Trump administration has asked a federal appeals court to dismiss its pre-election lawsuit challenging the certification of Democrat Mary Peltola's historic US Senate victory in Alaska.
content_html:
Justice Department Seeks Dismissal of Alaska Challenge

The Trump administration filed a motion asking a federal appeals court to declare its lawsuit moot, just two days after the Alaska Senate race was officially decided. The legal challenge, initiated prior to the midterm elections at the direction of Donald Trump, sought to block the certification of the race if Democrat Mary Peltola won.

The underlying dispute centered on the presence of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. Although the Alaska Supreme Court previously ruled that the second candidate's candidacy was entirely legal, the administration argued that a Peltola win should be delayed pending an investigation into potential voter confusion.

Key Details of the Senate Election

  • Mary Peltola won the election with 50.13% of the vote, securing more than the combined totals of incumbent Republican senator Dan Sullivan and a second Daniel Sullivan.
  • The Alaska Supreme Court previously ruled that the second Sullivan's candidacy was legal and that he could remain on the ballot.
  • The Trump administration's legal filing to drop the case came just one day after Alaska concluded its vote-count using ranked-choice tabulation.

Historic Win and Broader Ballot Controversies

Mary Peltola's victory carries profound national significance. As a member of the Yup’ik community, she will join Minnesota senator-elect Peggy Flanagan—a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe—as the first two Native American women to serve in the United States Senate.

The campaign trail in Alaska saw multiple controversies surrounding ballot configurations. Alongside the two Dan Sullivan candidates in the Senate race, the state's congressional contest featured Eric Hafner, an incarcerated federal prisoner in New York with no connection to Alaska, who managed to secure 22,715 votes after running as a Democrat.
